docs.title: iChidori-Crest
docs.text:
iChidori-Crest is a compact Raspberry Pi HAT designed for high-precision GNSS positioning and embedded applications. It integrates a Septentrio mosaic-G5 GNSS receiver module with an mPCIe interface for an LTE modem, onboard power management, SD card logging, and additional connectivity and expansion interfaces.

Designed for Raspberry Pi 4 and Raspberry Pi 5, iChidori-Crest provides a flexible hardware platform for RTK positioning, remote monitoring, and GNSS-based applications. It is available in variants — P1, P3, P3H, and P6 — sharing the same board hardware while offering different GNSS receiver capabilities.

docs.title: Powered by the Next-Generation Septentrio mosaic-G5
docs.text:
At the heart of iChidori-Crest is the Septentrio mosaic-G5, a new generation of ultra-compact, high-performance GNSS receiver modules. Combining multi-constellation, multi-frequency satellite tracking with centimeter-level RTK positioning, mosaic-G5 brings advanced positioning capabilities to space- and power-constrained systems.

Compared with the mosaic-X5, mosaic-G5 offers a 60% smaller module footprint and 40% lower power consumption, while maintaining high-precision positioning performance. Depending on the receiver variant, the series supports tracking of up to four frequencies, output rates of up to 100 Hz, and AIM+ Premium, advanced GNSS+ algorithms for enhanced resilience against interference and spoofing.

These capabilities make mosaic-G5 well suited for compact RTK systems, robotics, autonomous platforms, and other applications where positioning performance, reliability, size, and power efficiency are critical.

docs.title: GNSS Data Logger
docs.text: Log GNSS data locally on the Raspberry Pi while streaming corrections via LTE.

docs.title: Basic NMEA Logging
docs.text:
# Log NMEA from mosaic-G5 COM1 to file, timestamped
while true; do
    cat /dev/ttyAMA0 >> /home/pi/gnss-log-$(date +%Y%m%d).nmea
done

docs.title: Log with Rotation (logrotate)
docs.text:
Create /etc/logrotate.d/gnss:

/home/pi/gnss-log-*.nmea {
    daily
    rotate 7
    compress
    missingok
    notifempty
}

docs.title: SBF Binary Logging (mosaic-G5)
docs.text:
mosaic-G5 supports Septentrio Binary Format (SBF) for compact, precise logging.

Configure via mosaic-G5 web interface or COM1:

# Enable SBF output on COM1
setSBFOutput, COM1, PVTGeodetic+MeasEpoch, sec1

Then log:

cat /dev/ttyAMA0 > /home/pi/gnss-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).sbf &

docs.title: Systemd Service for Continuous Logging
docs.text:
# /etc/systemd/system/gnss-logger.service
[Unit]
Description=GNSS Data Logger
After=multi-user.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'cat /dev/ttyAMA0 >> /home/pi/gnss-$(date +%%Y%%m%%d).nmea'
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

sudo systemctl enable gnss-logger
sudo systemctl start gnss-logger

docs.title: LTE Sleep Mode
docs.text: Reduce power consumption by putting the LTE module to sleep when a network connection is not needed.

docs.title: GPIO Signals
docs.text: Signal GPIO Direction DTR GPIO20 Pi → LTE (HIGH = sleep request) WAKE# GPIO13 LTE → Pi (LOW = module awake)

docs.title: Sleep Mode — UART Interface (EC21-J / BG96)
docs.text:
When using UART (not USB), sleep requires two conditions:

  1. AT+QSCLK=1 — enable sleep mode via AT command
  2. DTR HIGH — assert DTR to signal sleep to module

USB not required

For UART-only setups, USB suspend is not needed. DTR + AT+QSCLK=1 is sufficient.

docs.title: Sleep Test Script
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
DTR_PIN=20
WAKE_PIN=13

echo "=== LTE Sleep Mode Test (UART) ==="

# Verify module is responsive before sleep
echo -e "AT\r" > /dev/ttyAMA3
sleep 1
RESPONSE=$(timeout 3 cat /dev/ttyAMA3 2>/dev/null)
echo "Pre-sleep AT response: $RESPONSE"

# Step 1: Enable sleep mode
echo "Step 1: AT+QSCLK=1"
echo -e "AT+QSCLK=1\r" > /dev/ttyAMA3
sleep 2

# Step 2: Assert DTR HIGH → module enters sleep
echo "Step 2: DTR HIGH (sleep request)"
pinctrl set $DTR_PIN op
pinctrl set $DTR_PIN dh

echo "Waiting 5 seconds — measure current now..."
sleep 5

# Verify: AT command should get no response (module asleep)
echo -e "AT\r" > /dev/ttyAMA3
SLEEP_RESPONSE=$(timeout 3 cat /dev/ttyAMA3 2>/dev/null)
if [ -z "$SLEEP_RESPONSE" ]; then
    echo "✓ Sleep confirmed: no AT response"
else
    echo "✗ Module still awake: $SLEEP_RESPONSE"
fi

# Wake: DTR LOW
echo "Step 3: DTR LOW (wake)"
pinctrl set $DTR_PIN dl
sleep 3

# Restore DTR HIGH (idle state after wake)
pinctrl set $DTR_PIN dh

# Verify wake
echo -e "AT\r" > /dev/ttyAMA3
sleep 1
WAKE_RESPONSE=$(timeout 3 cat /dev/ttyAMA3 2>/dev/null)
echo "Post-wake AT response: $WAKE_RESPONSE"

Save as ~/lte-sleep-test.sh and run:

chmod +x ~/lte-sleep-test.sh
~/lte-sleep-test.sh

docs.title: BG96 — PSM and eDRX (Cat M1)
docs.text:
BG96 supports Power Saving Mode (PSM) and extended Discontinuous Reception (eDRX), which provide deeper sleep than DTR-based sleep.

Carrier support required

PSM and eDRX require network/carrier support. Verify with your carrier before configuring.

docs.title: Enable PSM
docs.text:
AT+CPSMS=1,,,"00000001","00000001"

Timer format (3GPP T3412 / T3324):

  • 00000001 = 2 seconds per unit × 1 unit = 2 seconds active timer
  • Adjust per your application duty cycle

docs.title: Enable eDRX
docs.text:
AT+CEDRXS=2,4,"0010"
  • Mode 2 = eDRX enabled + report unsolicited result
  • AcT-type 4 = LTE-M
  • eDRX value 0010 = 20.48 seconds

docs.title: Check Current PSM/eDRX Settings
docs.text:
AT+CPSMS?
AT+CEDRXS?
AT+CEDRXRDP

See also: EC21-J Datasheet, BG96 AT Commands Manual

docs.title: Two-Pi Relay
docs.text: Use two Raspberry Pi units: one in the field with iChidori-Crest (GNSS + LTE), one in the office as an NTRIP caster or relay server.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
[Field Pi]                    [Office Pi / VPS]
iChidori-Crest                NTRIP Caster (str2str)
  mosaic-G5                         ↑
     ↓ NMEA/SBF                RTCM relay
  str2str                           ↑
     ↓ NTRIP push           [RTK Client (rover)]
  LTE (ppp0)
     ↓ internet (Tailscale)
  [Office Pi]

docs.title: Field Pi: Push GNSS Stream
docs.text:
str2str \
  -in serial://ttyAMA0:115200 \
  -out ntrip://user:pass@office-pi:2101/FIELD1

docs.title: Office Pi: Run NTRIP Caster
docs.text:
Install RTKLIB str2str as caster:

str2str \
  -in ntrip://user:pass@office-pi:2101/FIELD1 \
  -out ntrips://:2101/RELAY1

docs.title: Connect via Tailscale
docs.text:
Both Pis are on the same Tailscale network. Use Tailscale IPs:

str2str \
  -in serial://ttyAMA0:115200 \
  -out ntrip://user:pass@100.64.x.x:2101/FIELD1

No port forwarding required — Tailscale handles NAT traversal.

docs.title: 40-Pin Header (J1)
docs.text:
iChidori-Crest connects to the Raspberry Pi via the standard 40-pin header.

Connector type: 2×20, 2.54 mm Pin socket

Mating connector: Raspberry Pi 4/5 Model B built-in 40-pin header

docs.title: UART Interfaces Summary
docs.text:
Interface Raspberry Pi Mosaic G5 LTE Module G5 UART UART0/1 (GPIO14/15) COM1 — G5 UART UART4 (GPIO8/9/10/11) COM2 — LTE UART UART3 (GPIO4/5/6/7) — UART

Serial port configuration

Raspberry Pi 4/5 has UART0–UART5, but most are disabled by default and require additional configuration.

For example to enable Pi UART GPIO14/15 to communicate with Mosaic G5 COM1:

  1. Run sudo raspi-config → Interface Options → Serial Port
  2. Select Interface Options → Serial Port
  3. Set Login shell over serial → No
  4. Set Serial port hardware → Yes
  5. Exit and reboot

Identify the UART Device: After reboot, check the serial device aliases. 

ls -l /dev/serial*
List available UART devices: 
ls -l /dev/ttyAMA* /dev/ttyS*
On Raspberry Pi 4/5, /dev/ttyAMA* represents PL011 UARTs; /dev/ttyS* represents mini UARTs.

Pin Signal Description 1 PI_GPIO13 Raspberry Pi GPIO13 2 LTE_WAKE# LTE modem wake signal (active low) 3 PI_GPIO12 Raspberry Pi GPIO12 4 +3V3 3.3V power 5 WP EEPROM Write protect 6 GND Ground

docs.title: USB device Interface (J5)
docs.text:
Connector type: USB Type-C, USB 2.0

The USB-C connector serves as the primary power supply and data interface.

An internal 2-port USB hub routes the single connector to two independent device interfaces:

Port Connected Device 1 Mosaic G5 USB device interface 2 LTE mPCIe USB device interface

docs.title: GNSS Antenna Connectors
docs.text:
iChidori-Crest provides two MMCX antenna ports for the mosaic-G5 receiver.

Antenna supply voltage

Both ports supply V_ANT = 3.3 V DC to power active GNSS antennas.

docs.title: Antenna Mode Setting
docs.text:
iChidori-Crest is offered in variants that differ in antenna capability:

Variant Antenna Mode P1, P3 Single-antenna only P3H, P6 Single-antenna or dual-antenna (heading)

Use the following commands to check or configure the antenna mode (needs to be done only once):

  • getFrontendMode — query the current antenna mode
  • setFrontendMode, SingleAnt — configure single-antenna mode at the next reboot
  • setFrontendMode, DualAnt — configure dual-antenna (heading) mode at the next reboot
  • exeCopyConfigFile, Current, Boot — save the configuration to the boot file
  • exeResetReceiver, Hard, none — reboot to apply

Connect an active antenna to ANT_1 (MAIN). The ANT_1 input is DC-biased and ESD-protected; an active antenna can be connected directly without additional components. Leave ANT_2 (AUX) open when operating in single-antenna mode.

docs.title: SD Logging (J4)
docs.text:
A physical SD card slot is provided for direct on-board logging by the mosaic-G5 receiver.

Note

This SD logging capability is intended for evaluation and debugging purposes only; it is not recommended for use in production/deployed systems.

docs.title: SIM Card (J10)
docs.text:
The board provides a Nano SIM socket for the LTE module.

SIM slot on the LTE card

If the installed LTE card has its own SIM slot, the SIM can be inserted directly into that slot instead of the Nano SIM socket on the HAT. This allows SIM sizes other than Nano (for example Micro or Mini, depending on the card) to be used. The supported SIM types therefore depend on the LTE card in use.

docs.title: QWIC Connector (J11)
docs.text:
A QWIC connector is provided for expansion I2C communication.

Pin Signal 1 GND 2 3.3V 3 SDA 4 SCL

docs.title: LTE Modules Tested
docs.text:
The iChidori-Crest has been tested with the following LTE modules:

LTE Module Category Interface Quectel EC21-J LTE Cat 1 USB + UART Quectel BG96 LTE Cat M1 / NB-IoT USB + UART

Other LTE modules should be work, provided they use a compatible mPCIe form factor and interface configuration.

Note

The mPCIe LTE I²C interface is not connected in the current board revision. Use USB or UART for LTE communication.
